story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Devils have won two in a row, while the Blues (7-7-1) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Tuesday. Going in, the Blues are sixth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth).

The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .573, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Devils (.667 on chances worth .745), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Blues (lowest) and the Devils (2nd lowest) both keep things calm after the whistle. The Blues have struggled on the power play (31st). They also get some of the league’s best looks (3rd), so their good looks will be harder to come by against the Devils. On the other side, the Devils keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and throw a lot of pucks at the net (3rd). The Devils’ power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 15 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals. The Devils’ scoring runs through Jack Hughes (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP), who has eight points in his last five games.

Jordan Binnington (1-3-0 / .845 SV% in 4 GS) has had a rough start to the season for St. Louis, but is expected to start. Connor Hellebuyck (3-0-0 / .900 SV% in 3 GS) is expected to go for New Jersey. Binnington has a .935 save percentage in six starts against the Devils, well above his usual .898. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to send Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Neighbours, Dvorský and Buchnevich.
